content:
Aisha Khan: FYI — CI failing across the org. GitHub Actions API 5xxs and packages can't be pulled. Hotfix pipeline for transactions is blocked at artifact publish. Anyone seeing the same?

incident-bot: Paging Ravi Desai (primary oncall). Severity request: urgent. Please ack.

Ravi Desai: acked. I'm seeing dozens of failed workflow runs flagged "Request failed with status code 502". GitHub status shows degraded performance for Actions and Packages: https://www.githubstatus.com/ (incident listed).

Taylor Morgan: Confirmed. Our CI logs show checkout + publish steps failing. Example from workflow: 
```
Error: POST https://uploads.github.com/repos/redwood-inference/.../packages: 502 Bad Gateway
```

Nina Gomez: Are our self-hosted runners able to run the entire pipeline end-to-end? If yes, we could bypass GH-hosted runners and push artifacts to an alternative registry.

Ravi Desai: Self-hosted runners are healthy. The problem is GitHub Package Registry and Actions API endpoints themselves (package publish/pulls). Some deploy workflows assume artifacts live in GH packages; so downstream steps that reference them by package URL fail.

Taylor Morgan: I'm going to try a quick workaround: build the artifact on a self-hosted runner and upload it to an S3 bucket (internal-artifacts/redwood/hotfix). Then modify the deploy job to fetch from S3 and run rollout manually.

deploy-bot: Starting rerun on runner pool 'self-hosted-prod' per request from Taylor...

Ravi Desai: Heads-up for CS: this affects a customer hotfix for payment-retry backoff (Acme Corp). If we can't deploy within 30m they'll escalate. Nina, can you coordinate a short customer note?

Nina Gomez: On it. Short message ready: "We're investigating a third-party outage (GitHub Actions/Packages) affecting our CI/CD. We're performing a manual deploy to restore service; will update in 30 minutes." Sending now.

Taylor Morgan: Manual build log: 
```
# on self-hosted
git fetch origin hotfix/payment-backoff
git checkout hotfix/payment-backoff
./gradlew assemble -Penv=prod
aws s3 cp build/libs/payment-service.jar s3://internal-artifacts/redwood/hotfix/payment-service-2026-03-15.jar
```
Upload succeeded.

Ravi Desai: How about image registry? Our deploy pulls container images from GHCR for canary jobs. Can we retag and push to Docker Hub or GCR?

Taylor Morgan: Pushed image to Docker Hub (redwoodinc/payment-service:hotfix-2026-03-15). Updated k8s manifest locally.

deploy-bot: Manual deploy command requested by Ravi: 
```
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/payment-service payment-service=redwoodinc/payment-service:hotfix-2026-03-15
kubectl rollout status deploy/payment-service -n prod
```

Ravi Desai: Rollout in progress. Watching logs for initialization/migrations. Note: our migration job fetches a helper library from GitHub Packages; if that fails the migration might not start. We need to ensure the migration binary is baked into the image.

Taylor Morgan: I rebuilt the image with migrations included. Verified on staging.

Ravi Desai: Prod rollout complete, pods ready. Transaction rate normalizing. Quick impact summary: Acme experienced degraded payment throughput for ~35 minutes; retries succeeded, no data loss.

Nina Gomez: Sent customer update: service restored via manual deploy; we're doing a full investigation and will share a postmortem.

incident-bot: Created incident record PD-2026-0315-42 and internal tracker INF-2026-0315-github-packages. Assigned to Ravi Desai.

Aisha Khan: action items: 
- Short-term: document steps to use self-hosted runners + alternative registries during GH outages (owner: Taylor).
- Mid-term: add automatic fallback to internal artifact bucket and alternate image registry for critical pipelines (owner: Ravi).
- Postmortem: owner Nina, draft due in 72 hours.

Ravi Desai: I'll stay on the page for 20 more minutes then hand off monitoring to Taylor. Taylor, escalate to infra manager if GitHub hasn't recovered within 2 hours.

Taylor Morgan: acknowledged. I'll also open an RFC for adding artifact-fallback logic to our CI templates.

ops-bot: Uploading job logs and artifacts to incident folder: /incidents/INF-2026-0315-github-packages/logs (build, push, deploy).

Nina Gomez: Good job team. We should capture the root cause once GitHub posts their final timeline and check if any of our workflows contributed to the impact.

Ravi Desai: closing active mitigation notes here. Will keep incident open until vendor resolves and we complete postmortem."
